| `event` | `event` | `string` | No | No | A Pinterest tag event. Optional for VISITOR `audience_type`. Possible values are `pagevisit`, `signup`, `checkout`, `viewcategory`, `search`, `addtocart`, `watchvideo`, `lead`, and `custom`. This field also accepts a partner-defined Pinterest tag event. |

This object lists all the available predefined event data fields in the Pinterest tag. Besides what’s listed, you can also create your own set of `event_data` fields and define their usages or purposes according to your website needs. However, the benefit of using the predefined event data fields is that we can provide various metrics based on those fields' data. Examples per `event` type: `pagevisit` "event_data": &#123; "page_name": "My online store 123 \| view items \| shoe" &#125; `signup` "event_data": &#123; "lead_type": "New release promotion" &#125; `checkout` "event_data": &#123; "value": 116, "order_quantity": 2, "currency": "USD", "line_items": [ &#123; "product_name": "Pillows (Set of 2)", "product_id": "11", "product_price": 48, "product_quantity": 1 &#125;, &#123; "product_name": "Pillows, Large (Set of 2)", "product_id": "15", "product_price": 68, "product_quantity": 1 &#125; ] &#125; `addtocart` "event_data": &#123; "value": 499, "order_quantity": 1, "currency": "USD", "line_items": [ &#123; "product_name": "Red leather boots", "product_id": "3486", "product_category": "shoe", "product_variant_id": "JB11103000", "product_price": 499, "product_quantity": "1", "product_brand": "My brand" &#125;]&#125; `watchvideo` "event_data": &#123; "video_title" : "My Product Video 01" &#125; `lead` "event_data": &#123; "lead_type": "Newsletter" &#125; |
| `event_source` | `event_source` | `Inline7563` | No | No | Optional for VISITOR. You can use it as a &#123;'=': [value]&#125;. Supported values are: web, mobile, offline |
| `ingestion_source` | `ingestion_source` | `Inline7564` | No | No | Optional for VISITOR. You can use it as a &#123;'=': [value]&#125;. Supported values are: tag, mmp, file_upload, conversions_api |
| `objective_type` | `objective_type` | `Array<string>` | No | No | Objective for engagement audience filter. |
| `percentage` | `percentage` | `string \| number` | No | No | Percentage should be 1-10. The targeted audience should be this % size across Pinterest. |
| `pin_id` | `pin_id` | `Array<string>` | No | No | IDs of engaged organic pins. Optional for ENGAGEMENT `audience_type`. For example, "pin_id:": ["34567"] |
| `prefill` | `prefill` | `boolean` | No | No | Optional for VISITOR `audience_type`. If `true`, the specified rule on existing engagement data is applied to pre-populate the audience. If `false`, the audience is empty at creation time. The default is `true`. |
| `retention_days` | `retention_days` | `number` | No | No | Number of days a Pinterest user remains in the audience. Optional for ENGAGEMENT and VISITOR `audience_type`. Accepted range is 1-540. Defaults to 180 if not specified. |
| `seed_id` | `seed_id` | `Array<number> \| Array<string>` | No | No | Audience ID(s). For ACTALIKE `audience_type`. |
| `url` | `url` | `Array<string>` | No | No | Optional for ENGAGEMENT or VISITOR `audience_type`. For ENGAGEMENT, it is the engaged pin's URL. For VISITOR, you can use it as a string or a &#123;operator: value&#125; object for filtering visitors based on conversion tag event URLs. Supported operators are [ =, !=, contains, not_contains]. Example 1: "url": "http://www.myonlinestore123.com/view_item/shoe" Example 2: "url": &#123;"contains": "/view_item/shoe"&#125; |
| `visitor_source_id` | `visitor_source_id` | `string \| Array<string>` | No | No | The conversion tag ID, or the Pinterest tag ID, that you use on your website. For VISITOR `audience_type`. |

Examples per `event` type: `pagevisit` "event_data": &#123; "page_name": "My online store 123 \| view items \| shoe" &#125; `signup` "event_data": &#123; "lead_type": "New release promotion" &#125; `checkout` "event_data": &#123; "value": 116, "order_quantity": 2, "currency": "USD", "line_items": [ &#123; "product_name": "Pillows (Set of 2)", "product_id": "11", "product_price": 48, "product_quantity": 1 &#125;, &#123; "product_name": "Pillows, Large (Set of 2)", "product_id": "15", "product_price": 68, "product_quantity": 1 &#125; ] &#125; `addtocart` "event_data": &#123; "value": 499, "order_quantity": 1, "currency": "USD", "line_items": [ &#123; "product_name": "Red leather boots", "product_id": "3486", "product_category": "shoe", "product_variant_id": "JB11103000", "product_price": 499, "product_quantity": "1", "product_brand": "My brand" &#125;]&#125; `watchvideo` "event_data": &#123; "video_title" : "My Product Video 01" &#125; `lead` "event_data": &#123; "lead_type": "Newsletter" &#125; |

| `prefill` | `prefill` | `boolean` | No | No | Optional for VISITOR `audience_type`. If `true`, the specified rule on existing engagement data is applied to pre-populate the audience. If `false`, the audience is empty at creation time. The default is `true`. |

For VISITOR, you can use it as a string or a &#123;operator: value&#125; object for filtering visitors based on conversion tag event URLs. Supported operators are [ =, !=, contains, not_contains]. Example 1: "url": "http://www.myonlinestore123.com/view_item/shoe" Example 2: "url": &#123;"contains": "/view_item/shoe"&#125; |
